title: Argument-sensitive semantic compatibility over declarative relation metadata
independentExamples: A nonce landmark remains to the left after both endpoint names are replaced
A nonce contained object follows its container while an independently supported object does not
A renamed material class supports a declared action affordance while a contrasting class rejects it
outputTypes: inverse, implication, transition, affordance, and numeric witnesses
preconditions: finite statements and finite rule inventory
invariants: entity names remain data and never select control flow
relation arguments, polarity, inverse direction, and transition order are preserved
benchmark identifiers, item identifiers, answer indices, and complete benchmark sentences are absent from core
domain vocabulary is declarative KB metadata rather than source-code dispatch
a contradictory frame contributes negative evidence rather than being silently ignored
uncertaintySemantics: Compatibility is graded defeasible evidence. Equal aggregate scores remain a tie; absence of matching semantic evidence does not become a fabricated fact.
proofBehavior: Every contribution identifies the context frame, target frame, relation transform or KB affordance, signed contribution, and derivation path.
kbMigration: Adds an authored world-relations package and source-specific public providers. Existing package and runtime question behavior remain compatible.
